title: db.redis.apply — converge one Redis / Valkey instance (feature db.redis)
description: Converges one instance of the distribution's template unit <engine>-server@falak-<name>, its config /etc/falak-<engine>/<name>.conf (0640 root:<instance group>; the drop-in points ExecStart at it because Debian's /etc/redis is 0770 redis:redis). Each instance runs as its own system user (falak-<engine>-<name>, or falak-rh-/falak-vh-<hash> for long names; created on first apply with a Falak GECOS, and a same-named user Falak did not create is refused) through a drop-in /etc/systemd/system/<unit>.d/50-falak.conf that limits writes to its data directory /var/lib/falak-<engine>/<name> (0700) and its runtime directory. CONFIG is renamed to a random name only the agent knows; DEBUG, MODULE, SHUTDOWN, REPLICAOF, SLAVEOF, MIGRATE, ACL, MONITOR, SLOWLOG (and COMMANDLOG on Valkey 8.1+) are disabled. Memory limit, eviction, password and persistence change on the running instance; a new port, bind, drop-in or set of disabled commands restarts it: stop (save points set live first so the stop snapshots; none: snapshots off), files the new mode must not load moved aside, start. The current mode is asked from the running process (INFO persistence, CONFIG GET save), so a live AOF is never moved aside; switching to AOF never loads a stale AOF and never starts empty (AOF is switched on live after a start from dump.rdb with snapshots). Applies of one instance are serialized; waits end before the command's deadline. Fails with 'port N is in use by <process>' when another process holds a new port. Waits for PING (LOADING extends the wait). Idempotent: unchanged state is a no-op only once the running process is known to use it. The stock instance on 6379 is never touched. Feature db.redis.network adds `containers` and the bind checks.

password.description: requirepass of the default user. Written to the config file only; redis-cli gets it through REDISCLI_AUTH

bind.description: Addresses to listen on. 127.0.0.1 is always included; absent = 127.0.0.1 only. Only loopback, private (RFC 1918, CGNAT 100.64.0.0/10, IPv6 ULA fc00::/7) and WireGuard interface addresses are accepted (anything else fails the command, 0.0.0.0 / :: included); an accepted address the host does not have is left out and reported in `skipped`. Who can reach them is up to the firewall

containers.description: feature db.redis.network: also listen on the Docker default bridge's address (docker0, 172.17.0.1 out of the box), which every container on the server reaches through its network's gateway. Reported as container_host; nothing when Docker is not installed

persistence.description: rdb: snapshots (save 3600 1, 300 100, 60 10000); aof: append-only file, fsync every second, no snapshots; none: in memory only, every restart starts empty

changed.description: true when the configuration changed or the instance was (re)started

bind.description: feature db.redis.network: the addresses the instance listens on

container_host.description: feature db.redis.network: docker0's address when `containers` was asked and the bridge exists

skipped.description: feature db.redis.network: requested addresses the host does not have (yet)
